sections.h2: Which law governs renting a house in Oklahoma?
sections.html:
The Oklahoma Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, found at 41 O.S. 101 and following, sets the main rules for residential rentals. It dates from 1978, and section 135 directs courts to read it liberally so its purposes are carried out.

Older sections of Title 41, such as the ones on tenancy periods and notices to quit, sit alongside it. A landlord selling a rented house has to read both, because together they cover deposits, repairs, entry and what a sale does to the tenant's rights.

Oklahoma has 77 counties and about 3.96 million people as of 2020. Oklahoma County has 822,125 residents and Tulsa County has 698,782, so a good share of rental sales happen under those two county courts. The act is statewide, but each county court handles its own docket.

A landlord must keep the deposit in an escrow account at a federally insured institution in Oklahoma. Under 41 O.S. 115(A), misappropriating it is unlawful and can bring up to six months in county jail and a fine of up to twice the amount taken.

When the tenancy ends, a landlord who wants to keep any part must return the balance, without interest, within 45 days after termination, delivery of possession and the tenant's written demand. An itemized written statement must explain whatever was kept.

  • The tenant needs to make a written demand, even when no refund is expected.
  • If no demand is made within six months after the tenancy ends, the deposit reverts to the landlord.
  • A tenant may not treat the deposit as last month's rent unless the landlord agrees.

sections.h2: Repairs and what a tenant can do
sections.html:
Under 41 O.S. 118(A) the landlord must keep the unit fit to live in and keep the electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air conditioning that the landlord supplies in working order. Some duties do not apply to single-family homes, such as common-area upkeep, trash containers and supplying water and heat.

For a single-family house the tenant usually pays for utilities and trash service and cares for the lawn unless the lease says otherwise. In any home, the two sides may agree in a conspicuous separate writing that the tenant will do specified repairs or maintenance.

Tenant remedyWhat the tenant must do
Repair and deductWritten notice, then 14 days; the statute text caps the cost at under $100 (41 O.S. 121(B))
Repair or move outWritten notice that the tenant will leave 30 days after notice if the problem is not fixed in 14 days
Unlivable homeWritten notice and move out right away
Essential services cut offWritten notice, then end the rental, fix and deduct, sue for the difference or move and stop paying for that period

The $100 cap in older statute text may have been replaced with one month's rent, so confirm the current cap before relying on a dollar figure.

sections.h2: When can a landlord enter the house?
sections.html:
A landlord must give at least one day's notice before entering, which is commonly described as 24 hours, except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable. Entry must be at reasonable times. Section 128 lists the permitted purposes: inspections, necessary or agreed repairs, agreed services, and showing the unit to prospective buyers, lenders, tenants, workers or contractors.

The tenant may not unreasonably refuse. A landlord who is refused may seek an injunction or end the rental agreement. In the other direction, section 124 lets a tenant seek an injunction or end the rental, and recover actual damages, if the landlord enters unlawfully or harasses with repeated demands.

An owner lining up photos or buyer visits should send the notice in writing and offer a few time windows.

A landlord cannot lock a tenant out or cut off services to force a move. A landlord who wrongfully removes or excludes a tenant owes damages of up to twice the average monthly rent or twice actual damages, whichever is greater, under 41 O.S. 123. The tenant can recover possession through a court case, or end the rental and get deposits and unearned rent back.

The landlord must first send a summons and let the tenant appear in court before moving them out. An owner who wants a house vacant for a sale has to use the court process or negotiate a move-out.

The length of the rental decides the notice. If the agreement does not fix a definite term in writing, the tenancy is month-to-month, or week-to-week for a roomer or boarder paying weekly.

  • Month-to-month or at-will: 30 days written notice from either side (41 O.S. 111).
  • Shorter than month-to-month: 7 days written notice.
  • Fixed term: ends on its date without notice unless the parties agreed otherwise.
  • Unpaid rent: 5 days after written demand (41 O.S. 131).

A holdover tenant who stays without consent after the term ends can be sued for possession and damages. If the holdover is willful and not in good faith, the landlord may recover up to twice the average monthly rent for each month.

sections.h2: What happens to the lease when the landlord sells?
sections.html:
The lease continues with the new owner. Under 41 O.S. 119, a conveyance by a landlord is valid without the tenant's consent, and rent paid to the seller before written notice of the sale is good against the buyer.

Once the tenant gets written notice, rent goes to the successor. The seller is released from obligations for later events, and the successor is liable for every obligation under the rental agreement. Section 114 adds that successors of landlords and tenants have the same rights, duties and remedies as the people they replace.

Hand the buyer the deposit records too. Oklahoma's flood rule also follows the house: if the premises flooded in the past five years and the landlord knew, section 113a requires that to be stated prominently in writing in any written rental agreement, or the tenant can sue for personal property damage from flooding.

sections.h2: Abandoned property and a tenant's death
sections.html:
Two sections cover the awkward cases. When a tenant abandons the unit or is lawfully removed, 41 O.S. 130 lets the landlord dispose of items with no apparent value. For valuable items it requires a certified mail notice, and property left 30 days or more is deemed abandoned.

When a sole occupant dies, 41 O.S. 130.1 lets a landlord store the property and hand it to the contact the tenant named, who signs an inventory. The landlord may discard it only after a mailed request goes unanswered for 30 days after the postmark, and must refund the deposit less lawful deductions to the right person.

An heir who inherits a tenant-occupied house inherits these duties, and probate timing can make them harder to meet.

sections.h2: Selling a rented house in Oklahoma
sections.html:
Selling to a buyer who takes the house with the tenant in place avoids a forced move-out, because the lease carries over under section 119. Owners who need the house empty face a slower path, so it helps to work out early which of these applies:

  • Month-to-month tenants who are owed 30 days of written notice.
  • Deposits that have to be accounted for within 45 days after the tenant's demand.
  • Entry limits when buyers or appraisers want a showing.
  • Repair disputes, for example after storm damage to a roof, that can stall a closing.

A workable order of steps: read the lease for its term and any repair agreement, send written entry notices for each showing, write down the deposit balance, and give the tenant written notice of the sale once a contract is signed. A cash sale as-is skips repairs and showings for a buyer who plans to keep the lease.

faqs.q: How long does a landlord have to return a security deposit in Oklahoma?
faqs.a: 45 days after the tenancy ends, possession is delivered and the tenant makes a written demand. A landlord who keeps part must send an itemized statement under 41 O.S. 115(B), and an unclaimed deposit reverts to the landlord after six months.

faqs.q: How much notice must a landlord give before entering a rented house?
faqs.a: At least one day, except in an emergency or where notice is impracticable. Under 41 O.S. 128 the landlord may enter at reasonable times for inspections, repairs and showing the home to prospective buyers.

faqs.q: Can a tenant withhold rent for repairs in Oklahoma?
faqs.a: Only through the steps the statute allows. A tenant must give written notice, wait 14 days and then may deduct the cost of a qualifying repair, so simply refusing to pay is not safe. A tenant who calls the home unlivable cannot keep living there and refuse rent.

faqs.q: What happens to a tenant's lease if the owner sells the house?
faqs.a: The lease stays in force. The buyer takes over the landlord's obligations under 41 O.S. 119, and the tenant pays rent to the buyer once they have written notice of the sale.

faqs.q: Can a landlord change the locks if rent is late?
faqs.a: No. A landlord who excludes a tenant without a court order can owe up to twice the average monthly rent or twice actual damages, whichever is greater, under 41 O.S. 123.
